display.purpose: The day's verdict and page titles; one per screen.

headline.purpose: What matters / Also worth a look; alert day heads at 1rem.

title.purpose: The human one-line headline on a company card (1.125rem 600, 1.3): the largest thing on the card, above the 0.875rem company name and the 0.75rem ticker line.

body.purpose: Row headlines, expanded detail, results tables.

meta.purpose: Ticker, event and time lines; hints; source lines (ink-2).

label.purpose: Chip text, figure labels, table column heads.

shadows.name: segment-lift
shadows.purpose: Selected window segment only. The system is otherwise flat.

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: The one curve for everything; Tailwind's ease-out is overridden to it.

motion.name: expand
motion.purpose: Expand / collapse via grid rows 0fr to 1fr plus opacity; chevrons rotate in step; closed content is inert.

motion.name: press
motion.purpose: Cards tint paper-2 and settle to 0.99 scale; rows tint paper-2.

motion.name: badge-pop
motion.purpose: The alert count badge when it changes.

motion.name: sparkline-draw
motion.purpose: Sparklines and research charts draw in left to right once per visit. Nothing over 250ms; no page entrances or staggered lists; reduced motion respected.

breakpoints.name: column
breakpoints.purpose: Max content width; phone layout centres on wider screens. Designed at 390px.

sectorTint.purpose: Monogram avatar tint hashed from the sector name, never per ticker.

logoGreens.purpose: The FINN mark's five rays, light to dark. Logo, app icon and favicon only: green means 'up' in this UI, so it never becomes an accent.

narrative.overview:
A sharp printed brief, not a trading terminal: warm paper, near-black ink, one deep ink-blue accent, and a serif verdict at the top that says in one sentence what the day needs ("Tata Power and Bajaj Finance need a look today." / "Results season: 18 of 20 reported."). Everything under the verdict exists to justify it. The pre-build intent (calm, dense, editorial, read over morning chai) survived the build intact.

What changed after the user's phone review: the company is the unit, not the filing. Each company appears once per window, led by its most important filing (results > management change > fund raise > ...), with the rest folded behind "+N more filings", results documents folded into the results item, and every other material (P1) filing surfaced as its own one-line "Also" so it can never hide; the "+N more filings" fold inside the expanded card holds only P2/P3. Material companies get a rich card; the rest get a compact row. This deliberately replaced the original "2-line hairline rows, never boxed cards" rule for the top tier: a phone-sized card with numbers and a sparkline answered "does it matter?" faster than a row did. Hairline rows remain the grammar everywhere below the top tier.

Density is phone-first (390px) and calm: one column, max 36rem, nothing decorative. Colour is information, not mood.
keyCharacteristics: Serif verdict, sans everything else, tabular figures throughout.
Two tiers: "What matters" cards (max 6, then "Show N more companies"), "Also worth a look" rows; routine filings collapsed into one row.
Green/red only on signed numbers; ink-blue only on interactive or "material" marks.
Forced light scheme: the paper is the identity, so the browser may not dark-repaint it.
Flat paper; the only shadow is a 1px lift on the selected window segment.

rules.name: The Number-Only Rule
rules.body: Green and red touch the signed figure and nothing else. If a row is coloured, it is wrong.

rules.name: The One Ink Rule
rules.body: Ink-blue means "you can act on this" or "this is material". It never decorates.

rules.name: The Paper Stays Paper Rule
rules.body: color-scheme: only light on the root and in the viewport. There is no dark theme; do not add dark: variants.

rules.name: The Serif Judges Rule
rules.body: Serif is reserved for sentences that state a verdict or name a section. Data, labels and controls are always sans.

rules.name: The Weight Not Colour Rule
rules.body: Hierarchy comes from size and weight (400 / 500 / 600). No all-caps, no letter-spaced labels.

rules.name: The Paper Has No Shadows Rule
rules.body: Cards are separated by a hairline border and a lighter face, never a drop shadow.

dos: Do make the company the unit: one entry per company per window, lead item by priority, the rest folded.
Do cap "What matters" at 6 cards and put the rest behind one "Show N more companies" tap.
Do colour only the signed percentage, via Signed.
Do keep every target at 44px or more and pad the fixed bars for safe areas.
Do cite the source on every expanded item ("Open filing at p. N").
Do derive avatar tints from sector, never from the ticker.
donts: Don't add drop shadows to cards, gradients, glassmorphism or coloured backgrounds.
Don't use emoji, icon fonts or decorative icons; icons are only the four authored tab glyphs and chevrons.
Don't use all-caps labels, eyebrows or kickers above headings.
Don't write long LLM paragraphs or "insight" filler; headlines are one line with numbers copied from the filing.
Don't add a dark theme or let the browser force one.
Don't repeat "Reaction pending" on rows; it is one banner.
